items.title: California DMV bars Waymo AVs from operating on the state’s freeways
items.summary: The California DMV has barred Waymo autonomous vehicles from operating on state freeways due to safety concerns. This action followed incidents where Waymo vehicles entered active construction closures and interacted with law enforcement. The DMV determined that freeway operations posed an imminent hazard due to incursions into construction zones. Waymo will remain restricted until it demonstrates corrective actions addressing these deficiencies. Waymo stated that the ban only applies to freeways, and its service continues safely on city streets.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "California DMV bars Waymo AVs from operating on the state’s freeways". This segment details the California Department of Motor Vehicles' action to restrict Waymo autonomous vehicles from operating on state freeways following safety concerns. The DMV determined that freeway operations presented an imminent hazard due to Waymo vehicles entering active construction closures and interacting with law enforcement personnel. This restriction was implemented because of specific incidents where Waymo vehicles entered areas under construction and engaged with law enforcement activity. Waymo indicated that the ban is limited to freeways, maintaining service on city streets. The company stated that the restriction remains in place pending demonstration of corrective actions addressing these identified deficiencies. The industry will observe the implementation of these corrective measures by Waymo to determine future operational parameters.

items.title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need
items.summary: Humyn Labs raised $47 million in Series A funding to supply real-world data for training U.S. robotics and AI companies. The company uses two-camera hardware to record and process footage of people performing everyday tasks across over 20 countries. Humyn Labs collects data on actions, hand movements, and object interactions to create usable AI training sets. The startup generates revenue primarily from U.S. customers, including AI labs and robotics companies. The initiative raises important considerations regarding privacy and consent in data collection.
items.audio_script: From TechCrunch - Robotics, India’s Humyn Labs raises forty-seven million dollars in Series A funding to supply real-world data for training U.S. robotics and artificial intelligence companies. This process involves collecting data concerning actions, hand movements, and object interactions to construct usable sets for artificial intelligence training. Revenue generation primarily stems from U.S. clientele, including robotics firms and AI research laboratories. The initiative brings into focus critical considerations regarding privacy and consent in large-scale data collection practices. This development signals an emerging trend in the provision of cross-national, real-world data essential for advancing robotics and AI model development.

items.title: Genesis AI raises $500M to deploy glove-wearing robots
items.summary: Genesis AI raised $500 million in a Series A round to advance its glove-wearing robot technology. The company has demonstrated complex manipulation skills through its physical AI model operating robotic arms. Genesis gathers force data using sensor-enabled gloves worn by workers to train its model. The company focuses on vertical integration, developing its own data, AI model, and humanoid robot design. The primary bottleneck for Genesis is achieving industrial-grade hardware and sufficient real-world data for generalized robotic intelligence.

items.title: THG Fulfil doubles AutoStore capacity at Warrington warehouse
items.summary: THG Fulfil has doubled the storage capacity of its Omega warehouse in Warrington to 240,000 bins. This expansion increases the AutoStore storage capacity at the Omega to 8.4 million units, supported by more robots and carousel ports. This automated infrastructure addresses retailer pain points related to rising labor costs and customer satisfaction. The system allows brands to manage hypergrowth and absorb volume spikes while maintaining speed and accuracy. THG Fulfil is uniquely positioned as both a distributor and an active end-user of AutoStore technology globally.

items.title: Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries expand Spot operations and prepare to test Atlas humanoid
items.summary: Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries are expanding Spot deployments for autonomous asset management across GlobalFoundries' semiconductor fabrication sites in multiple locations. GlobalFoundries will also be the first non-automotive customer to begin testing the Atlas humanoid robot as part of an early adopter program. Spot has already helped GF shift to predictive maintenance by collecting data across inspection points in their fabs. The collaboration aims to scale Spot and test Atlas to advance AI-enabled manufacturing globally. Testing of Atlas at GF facilities is scheduled to begin in early 2027 to evaluate use cases and integration needs.

items.title: Groundworks 2026 calls for faster adoption of construction robotics in UK
items.summary: Groundworks 2026 convened leaders to explore deploying construction robotics on active sites to address the labor gap. Discussions emphasized that successful adoption requires planning suitable tasks early, establishing a viable supply chain, and building client confidence through real project evidence. Speakers demonstrated how automation can boost productivity and support stretched teams while accounting for site-specific conditions. Wider adoption necessitates testing robotics against daily site changes and focusing on solutions built around specific tasks. The event brought together industry stakeholders, developers, investors, and policymakers to discuss the commercial and practical integration of robotics.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS Wiki Content Migration Effort
items.summary: A process was initiated to migrate documentation from the archived ROS wiki into README.md files for ROS packages. This involves creating a pipeline to extract package-specific content, convert it to Markdown, and aggregate it into proposed READMEs. The goal is to make this valuable documentation accessible in GitHub repositories for future developers. The effort involves manually reviewing and filtering content to ensure quality before opening pull requests against the noetic branch. This bulk migration aims to preserve essential ROS wiki information within the codebase.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS Wiki Content Migration Effort". A process was initiated to extract package-specific content, convert it to Markdown, and aggregate it into proposed READMEs through a pipeline. This effort requires manual review and filtering of the content to ensure quality before initiating pull requests against the noetic branch. The bulk migration seeks to preserve essential ROS wiki information directly within the codebase. This migration effort contributes to improved accessibility of foundational ROS knowledge within the development ecosystem.

items.title: Learn how AI is changing supply chain robotics
items.summary: Supply chain robotics is transforming operations to address labor shortages, improve efficiency, and build resilience. Current technologies include warehouse automation, autonomous mobile robots, and AI-powered inventory management. Artificial intelligence enables predictive analytics, demand forecasting, and dynamic routing to optimize robot performance. Integrating these systems allows for end-to-end supply chain optimization that adapts to changing demand and supports high-volume production. These advancements lead to higher quality, reduced downtime, and cost optimization for manufacturers.

items.title: Wildfire Tech is Automating Everything but the Hose
items.summary: Wildfire response is adopting automation through AI detection, aerial coordination, and autonomous suppression launchers. Ground-level operations, like moving water, remain challenging due to unstructured terrain and unpredictable variables. Electrifying equipment early, such as electric pumps, provides a controllable platform for future autonomy. Detection and coordination are established layers, while physical application remains the final, necessary step. The physical act of applying water is currently the last mile that resists full automation.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Wildfire Tech is Automating Everything but the Hose". This report details the integration of artificial intelligence, aerial coordination, and autonomous suppression launchers into wildfire response efforts, demonstrating progress in automation. The response strategy involves establishing detection and coordination layers utilizing AI for early detection and aerial management. Autonomous suppression launchers are being deployed for targeted application, while electric pumps are being trialed to provide a controllable platform for future automation. However, the physical act of moving water across unstructured terrain remains a significant challenge resistant to full autonomy. The current setup establishes advanced detection and coordination systems while acknowledging that physical application constitutes the final, necessary step in suppression operations. This indicates a focus on layered technological integration as the immediate bottleneck for complete autonomous response systems.

items.title: Ep#117: Residual Modeling Closes the Regression and Generative Policy Gap in Robot Learning
items.summary: Generative policies like diffusion and flow-matching often outperform direct action regression (MSE-Policies) in robot learning from demonstrations. This performance gap is attributed not primarily to multimodality, but to the mismatch in loss functions stemming from state-dependent variations in action residuals and heavy-tailed data. The authors propose HT-Policies, which learn input-dependent residual scales and incorporate a Student-t residual model to mitigate the influence of these heavy tails. HT-Policies achieve performance competitive with generative baselines while offering faster training and inference. This research suggests that accounting for residual distribution and scale is crucial for effective policy optimization in robot learning.
items.audio_script: From RoboPapers, "Ep#117: Residual Modeling Closes the Regression and Generative Policy Gap in Robot Learning" reports on a method that addresses a performance discrepancy in robot learning from demonstrations. The research demonstrates that generative policies often surpass direct action regression methods, and this gap is primarily linked to mismatches in loss functions arising from state-dependent action residuals and heavy-tailed data distributions. The authors introduced HT-Policies, a framework designed to learn input-dependent residual scales and incorporate a Student-t residual model to manage the effect of heavy tails in the data. These HT-Policies achieved performance comparable to generative baselines while exhibiting accelerated training and inference times. Accounting for the distribution and scale of the action residuals is shown to be a critical factor for effective policy optimization in robot learning systems. This research indicates a pathway toward more robust and efficient policy optimization in embodied AI.

items.title: Welcome, Spirit v1.5!
items.summary: Spirit v1.5 is an open-source robot foundation model developed by Spirit AI, released on January 12, 2026, in the vision-language-action category for robotics. It is software designed for integration into robotic systems, not a physical robot, and currently scores a Humanoid Guide Brain of 5 out of 10. The model was ranked first on RoboChallenge, an evaluation benchmark using real robots, demonstrating its capability. Training emphasizes collecting varied data from less scripted operator activity to enhance data diversity for faster learning. Spirit AI released the model and code openly to foster further development in home robot foundations.

items.title: Welcome, Quanta X1 Pro!
items.summary: The Quanta X1 Pro is a wheeled, humanoid research platform developed by X Square Robot, emphasizing mobile manipulation over legged movement. It measures 169 cm tall, weighs 80 kg, and features two arms and extensive camera arrays for sensing. The platform can perform tasks like sorting goods, assembling products, and obstacle avoidance using its wheeled mobility. It is equipped with onboard computing, AI models, and ROS2 support, targeting research, education, and industrial applications. The system has a developing overall skill score of 4/10, with stronger manipulation capabilities than navigation.

items.title: ClearSpace moves closer to launch of European space debris removal mission
items.summary: ClearSpace has secured an agreement with OHB System AG to provide navigation and capture technologies for the European Space Agency’s ClearSpace-1 mission. This mission aims to demonstrate the safe capture and removal of an unprepared object from Earth orbit. ClearSpace will develop the necessary technologies to approach, navigate, and capture objects in orbit. The mission will target the Proba-1 satellite to prove robotic capture capability for space debris removal. Furthermore, ClearSpace is developing commercial in-orbit servicing capabilities through other European space programs.

items.title: Technical Report of Auriga's 1:10 Scale Autonomous Vehicle Robot
items.summary: Auriga Robotics developed a 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle platform at Shahid Beheshti University. The system integrates a custom chassis with an embedded system based on ESP32 microcontrollers and a Jetson Orin NX module. The embedded layer handles real-time sensor interfacing and actuator control, while the Jetson manages deep-learning-based perception and trajectory control. The software stack utilizes ROS and control algorithms like Stanley, PID, and Pure Pursuit for navigation. This platform serves as a modular research base for autonomous driving studies.

items.title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
items.summary: A passage-focused framework is proposed for hierarchical multi-robot navigation in bottleneck environments by combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. It utilizes a passage-induced graph of convex sets for priority-ordered planning and passage-aware route selection. Route-restricted continuous space-time planning is used to penalize temporal conflicts, guiding a model predictive path integral controller. The system incorporates adaptive tracking and selective replanning to handle execution deviations while maintaining coordination. Experimental results show this framework achieves high success rates and outperforms baselines in makespan and flowtime.

items.title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
items.summary: Reinforcement learning for point-cloud grasping policies often leaves specific grasp failures unsolved despite optimizing for plausibility. The authors propose a human-in-the-loop failure loop to correct these persistent failures. When an RL policy fails, the specific situation is sent to a virtual reality application for a person to demonstrate the correct grasp. This human demonstration is then used to retrain the policy, effectively adding two grasp points. This method significantly boosts the success rate on hard cases, nearly doubling performance from 24% to 45% for those failed grasps.

items.title: Optimal Operating-Point Selection for Single-Linearization Trajectory Planning of Nonlinear Robot Manipulators
items.summary: The paper proposes an offline, performance-driven method for selecting an optimal single linearization point for trajectory planning of nonlinear robot manipulators. Candidate operating points are sampled from a cubic seed trajectory, and each yields an affine model used in a constrained quadratic program. The selected operating point is determined by minimizing the nonlinear trajectory objective after executing the resulting control sequences on the nonlinear dynamics. Evaluation on a three-DOF UR5 manipulator showed that this selection method reduced the nonlinear trajectory objective by significant amounts compared to conventional linearization methods. This systematic selection improves trajectory planning while maintaining a fixed affine planning model.

items.title: TMA: Sim-to-Real Forceful Humanoid Manipulation via Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation
items.summary: Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation (TMA) is a method for achieving zero-shot sim-to-real forceful humanoid manipulation by incorporating tactile feedback. It structures policy learning based on interactions observable through tactile feedback and uses cone geometry as a bias for multi-finger contact representation. The approach adapts motor behavior online from tactile history to handle real-world uncertainties in contact dynamics. TMA successfully demonstrated this by outperforming other baselines on real-world round doorknob opening tasks. The system coordinates upper-body manipulation with a pretrained locomotion controller for whole-body stability.

items.title: Robot Demonstration Videos Should Include Transparency Disclosures
items.summary: Public dissemination of robotics progress relies on curated demonstration videos, which the public struggles to evaluate for visual and behavioral authenticity. This lack of detail distorts public perception, causing overestimations of robot capabilities. The research proposes adopting disclosure standards for robot demonstration videos to enhance transparency. Including clear disclosures significantly improves public discernment regarding the visual and behavioral authenticity of these videos. Ultimately, these standards aim to accurately calibrate public expectations about robotics research.

items.title: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
items.summary: A frozen robot policy can allocate deployment-time inference compute either to refine a predicted action chunk or to initiate more frequent policy replans. The study evaluates this allocation strategy without updating model weights, using a SmolVLA checkpoint in LIBERO simulation. The evaluation considers both nominal compute rate and complete attempt cost across discovery and held-out tasks. Results show that the optimal allocation depends on evaluating generation effort and feedback frequency jointly, rather than a universal setting.
